claims.harm: Using Update() when not chaining can mask bugs where a fresh assignment is intended and hurts readability
claims.quote: I don't think this is good usage of Update(), since there is no chaining happening here. I would find list initialization more readable and less error-prone
claims.settled_by_quote: Also took suggestions to simplify usage in CompleteChainstateInitialization.

claims.harm: Adding unnecessary complexity to util::Result when simpler Expected or smaller patches could be used
claims.quote: My recommendation would be to keep the code as simple as possible and not add complicated features or complication that isn't required.

claims.harm: Conflating error return values with multi-message reporting when util::Expected should be prioritized
claims.quote: I think util::Result is conflating 2 related but orthogonal needs... At this point I would prefer util::Expected be merged first (#34006).
claims.settled_by_quote: The former makes it a clearer departure from util::Expected - warnings can be added and merged into parent results while still returning successful values.

claims.harm: LoadChainstate and VerifyLoadedChainstate do not use warnings or multiple errors, so applying util::Result to them is not well motivated over util::Expected
claims.quote: I maintain that the current example in this PR of applying util::Result to LoadChainstate & VerifyLoadedChainstate is not well motivated as they don't use warnings or multiple errors, and are thus a better fit for util::Expected
